title: Teaching
text:
R 语言 tidyverse 入门工作坊
An introduction to R and the tidyverse for beginners
This workshop is designed for those who have little to no experience with R (but with some experience in statistics), and covers the basics of data manipulation and visualization using the tidyverse packages. The workshop is taught in Chinese.

title: Slides
text:
Hands-on Copilot: Writing Stata in VS Code
上手 Copilot：在 VS Code 里写 Stata (original)
A hands-on introduction to using GitHub Copilot inside VS Code to write Stata — setting up the Stata extension and the Automation bridge, comment-driven inline completions, and a live World Values Survey workflow from data cleaning through regression. Lecture for the 15th Applied Social Science Methods Summer School (SHU), Data Analysis series, July 2026.


Say It, Done: AI Agents in Social Science Research
言出法随：社会科学研究中的 AI 智能体 (original)
A survey of AI agents for sociological research — what agents are and how they retrieve knowledge, the acceleration-versus-empowerment distinction, their capabilities and limits, and a practical guide to configuring and harnessing them in a research project. Lecture for the 15th Applied Social Science Methods Summer School (SHU), Data Analysis series, July 2026. The English version is adapted for international audiences.

title: Minghong Shen 沈明宏
text:
Minghong Shen is a Postdoctoral Fellow at the Population Studies Center at the University of Pennsylvania. His research broadly focuses on early childhood development, education, urban studies, artificial intelligence, and computational social science. He received his PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology in 2025 and was a postdoctoral fellow at NYU Shanghai before joining Penn.

title: Books
text:
Stata to R Reference
Stata 转 R 参考手册
A technical reference book for Stata users moving to R, available in English and Chinese. Nearly 1,800 paired examples across 41 chapters connect familiar commands with R approaches, helping readers apply what they already know while learning a different way of working.
The book serves as a practical companion to research, from preparing data to developing more advanced analyses. Readers can follow a topic in depth or consult individual examples as questions arise.


Claude Code 社会科学配置指南
A configuration guide for social science researchers
Written in collaboration with Xinyang Tang, this book introduces social science researchers (using R, Stata, and Python) to Claude Code (or other agentic AI tools) — from installation and daily use to advanced topics like sub-agents, MCP servers, and hooks. The book is written in Chinese.


tidyverse 入门
An introduction to tidyverse
This book is a work in progress. Unlike traditional textbooks, this book classifies the functions in the tidyverse as well as tidystata and explains them in a systematic way. The book is written in Chinese.

title: Software
text:
Stata to R Reference / Stata 转 R 参考手册
A searchable bilingual reference for Stata users working in R
Browse Stata–R comparisons by subject, command or R package. English and Chinese editions share the same examples, with a language switch on each chapter. The reference accompanies tidystata and is separate from the introductory textbook.

title: Software
text:
tidystata

This R package (formerly statart) combines Stata-inspired features with tidyverse-style operations for exploring and preparing data:

tab() and fre() return frequency tables as data frames.
summ() and tabstat() return summary statistics.
codebook(), variables(), misstable(), and pwcorr() inspect variables, missing values, and correlations.
isid(), assert(), and s_merge() check keys and merge data.
Row calculations, std(), as_dummy(), panel lags, and binning help prepare variables.
findit() gives the R equivalent of a Stata command.

Coming from Stata? See Coming from Stata. Install the development version with pak::pak("socimh/tidystata").
